Weighted aggregation of unit scores to larger units

Source: R/val.R
val_aggregate.Rd

Rolls scores for small units, such as census tracts, up to larger units, such as counties, as a weighted mean. Survey data often identify only the larger unit, so an index built for tracts has to be aggregated before it can be linked to respondents.

Usage

val_aggregate(data, by, value, weight, na_rm = FALSE)

Arguments

data

A data frame or sf object of small units. Geometry is dropped.

by

<tidy-select> One or more columns naming the larger unit each row belongs to. For census tracts the county is the first five characters of the tract GEOID.

value

<tidy-select> One numeric column of scores to aggregate.

weight

<tidy-select> One numeric column of non-negative weights, usually the population the score is for.

na_rm

If FALSE (the default), a group with any missing score gets a missing value. If TRUE, units with missing scores are left out, and the weight and unit count describe only the units used.

Value

A tibble with one row per group: the by columns, the weighted mean (named after value), the total weight (named after weight) and n_units, the number of units in the group.

Details

The value for group \(g\) is \(\sum_{i \in g} w_i v_i / \sum_{i \in g} w_i\). A group whose weights sum to zero has no defined mean; it gets NA and a message counts such groups. Groups with missing values in by are kept as their own group, as in dplyr::group_by().

Examples

tracts <- data.frame(
  county = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b"),
  access = c(10, 20, 40, 5, 15),
  youth = c(100, 100, 200, 300, 100)
)
val_aggregate(tracts, county, access, youth)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   county access youth n_units
#>   <chr>   <dbl> <dbl>   <int>
#> 1 a        27.5   400       3
#> 2 b         7.5   400       2
